Grow with us ASIC Quality Data Analyst Austin, Texas Hybrid, on-site work schedule Ericsson Silicon is expanding its custom ASIC capabilities for 5G Advanced and 6G. The Central Engineering ASIC Quality team supports product quality and reliability throughout the ASIC lifecycle. The analysis starts with factory failures and field returns and follows the evidence wherever it leads, including wafer fabrication, assembly, and test. Semiconductor expreience is required for this opening. We are looking for an ASIC Quality Data Analyst with strong AI and analytical capabilities to analyze factory and field failures, identify recurring failure signatures, and support root-cause investigations. The role brings together production test, manufacturing, repair, and field-return data to reduce the time needed to diagnose failures and establish root causes. The findings will also support test development and screening improvements that reduce defective parts per million (DPPM) and improve the quality of our products in the field. What you will do: You will own the analytical work supporting factory and field failure investigations, including data correlation, analytical tools, automated workflows, and reporting. You will work with internal factories, field organizations, Product Engineering, Test Engineering, Quality, and other engineering teams to develop evidence and evaluate failure hypotheses. Engineering and Quality owners remain responsible for confirming root causes, making containment decisions, and implementing corrective actions. You will also engage semiconductor fabs and external manufacturing partners as needed to trace failures across the supply chain and support corrective actions. Analyze factory production, test, repair, and field-return data to identify failure trends, recurring signatures, quality escapes, and emerging product risks. Work directly with internal factories and field organizations to collect and correlate failure evidence, prioritize analytical work with investigation owners, and support containment, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions. Collaborate with Product Engineering, Test Engineering, ASIC Design, Reliability, Quality, Manufacturing, Validation, and System Debug teams to investigate factory and field issues and validate technical findings. Develop and maintain tools, scripts, and analytical models that correlate factory and field data, identify recurring failure signatures, and prioritize hypotheses for engineering investigation. Build and maintain automated data pipelines linking factory test, manufacturing history, repair records, and field returns, with the traceability needed to follow failures back to production lots, devices, and processes. Apply statistical analysis and AI/ML techniques to detect abnormal failure patterns, group related returns, automate data analysis, and identify quality risks earlier. Use production yield, screening, defect, wafer fab, and assembly/test data to investigate factory and field failures, assess quality escapes, and evaluate the effectiveness of process or test changes. Develop dashboards and reporting tools to track factory failure rates, field returns, DPPM trends, recurring failure modes, and investigation progress, including time to diagnosis and root-cause confirmation. Document analytical findings, present supporting evidence, and work with engineering and factory teams to confirm root causes and measure the effectiveness of corrective actions and screening changes. Reduce the time needed to diagnose and root-cause factory and field failures by automating data preparation, correlating evidence across sources, and making relevant failure history available to investigation teams. Join our Team What you will bring: The ability to Identify failure modes contributing to factory defects and field escapes is critical in this role. Your experience providing failure signatures and analytical evidence to Product Engineering and Test Engineering to support test development and validation, reduce outgoing DPPM, and evaluate screening effectiveness, including escapes and false rejects is critical. Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Data Analytics, or a related field. 3–5 years of experience in data analytics, engineering analytics, data science, or a related role in a semiconductor environment. Hands-on experience with Python, SQL, data modeling, visualization, or comparable analytical tools. Practical experience using statistical methods and AI/ML techniques for data analysis or workflow automation. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including experience working with complex or inconsistent data from multiple sources. Ability to collaborate across engineering disciplines and communicate technical findings clearly. Experience in semiconductor manufacturing, factory test, product engineering, quality, reliability, failure analysis, or related hardware environments. Familiarity with manufacturing failure data, production test results, repair records, field returns, and device traceability; exposure to wafer fabrication or assembly processes is beneficial. Experience developing and maintaining analytical tools, automated workflows, anomaly-detection models, or predictive quality methods. Analytics & Insight Delivery

Google Analytics & Data Collection

Data Quality & Platform Collaboration

· Own the accuracy and freshness of all data products in scope. Proactively identify and investigate data quality issues — with root-cause evidence — and partner with Analytics Engineers and Data Engineers to resolve upstream problems promptly.

· Write high-quality, performant SQL — including complex window functions and CTEs — and collaborate with Data Engineers on query optimisation, compute cost efficiency, and derived table design for owned analytical workloads.

· Collaborate with Analytics Engineers on LookML architecture and semantic layer design for owned domains — providing analytical requirements that inform model design and validating that data models correctly reflect business logic.

· Partner with the Senior BI & AI Analyst on customer analytics definitions for segmentation, LTV, and churn use cases. Consume ML model outputs from the Data Science team and surface them accurately in dashboards and analytical narratives.

· Understand the structure of data pipelines feeding owned dashboards sufficiently to diagnose data freshness and quality issues, escalate to the correct team, and communicate resolution timelines to stakeholders.

Standards, Mentorship & Team Development

· Own coding standards and analytical best practices for the team — including SQL style guides, LookML conventions, documentation requirements, and PR review processes. Conduct structured code reviews that are substantive, consistent, and designed to build capability in Junior Analysts.

· Mentor Junior Data Analysts through paired analysis, direct feedback, and structured review. Track improvement over time. Escalate development needs or blockers to the Manager.

· Build and contribute reusable assets to shared team libraries — including SQL query patterns, LookML components, analysis frameworks, and documentation templates — reducing time-to-delivery for the entire team, not just own work.

· Contribute to at least one standards update, governance policy, or best-practice guide per year.

AI-Augmented Analytics & Self-Serve Agent Development

· Apply LLM and AI tools (Gemini, GPT-4, Cortex Analyst, or equivalent) hands-on to accelerate analytics workflows — including automated insight narration, anomaly detection and explanation, and AI-assisted dashboard annotation. Practical delivered experience required; theoretical familiarity is not sufficient.

· Design and build self-serve analytics agents that enable non-technical stakeholders in Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, and Account Management to query data and surface insights in natural language — without raising tickets or requiring analyst intervention. Own the full lifecycle from prompt design through output validation and iteration.

· Configure Cortex Analyst or equivalent AI-assisted BI platforms to extend self-service beyond traditional dashboard interaction — including semantic model templates and YAML definitions that produce accurate, governed responses to unstructured business questions.

· Define quality standards for AI-generated analytical outputs — including accuracy validation, hallucination detection, and a review process before AI-generated insights are shared externally or with executives.

· Prototype and propose AI tooling that reduces repetitive analytical work for the team. Present prototypes to the Manager with a clear build-vs-buy recommendation and documented lessons learned that contribute to the team's shared AI analytics playbook.
